label: John Olsen Lear
narrative: John Lear is the rare figure in this cluster whose ordinary career is fully documented and whose extraordinary claims are not. He was born on 3 December 1942, the son of William Powell Lear, founder of Lear Jet, and Moya Olsen Lear, and his papers sit inside the William P. and Moya Olsen Lear Family Collection at The Museum of Flight Archives. In May 1966 he was one of the pilots on a Learjet 24 flight around the world that set a large number of international records. His place in this cluster is chronological as much as evidentiary: his own public claim document is dated 29 December 1987, roughly eighteen months before Lazar reached KLAS-TV, and it circulated through the ParaNet bulletin board in early 1988, setting the frame that Lazar's 1989 account then fitted into. He and Lazar had met by 1988, and he was present at the first and third of the three Wednesday-night desert viewings in the spring of 1989, on 22 March and 5 April, the second of which ended with the group detained by the Lincoln County Sheriff. He is carried here as an early promoter and a viewing participant, not as an eyewitness to any facility. He died on 29 March 2022.
